newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch credit insurer NCM opens two foreign units.
newsitem.headline: Dutch credit insurer NCM opens two foreign units.

text.p: Dutch NCM, among the five biggest credit insurers in Europe, said on Thursday it was planning to open offices in Germany and France.
Outside the Netherlands, NCM is already present in the United Kingdom, the United States, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Belgium and Israel.
"Our market share in Germany is only tiny," said NCM Chairman Maarten Hulshoff, adding this would change.
NCM has a market share of about 50 percent in the Scandinavian countries, 73 percent in the Benelux (Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg) and 40 percent in the United Kingdom.
Earlier on Thursday, NCM reported 1996 net profits of 14.2 million guilders versus a loss of 4.8 million guilders in 1995.
NCM said that volumes for credit insurers were increasing, but margins were under pressure as competition was getting harder.
"We have to work harder to earn the same amount of money," Hulshoff said.
NCM said it was too early to give a forecast for 1997.
